does: Fries a crumbed cutlet whole in deep oil, turning it once, until the crust is deep gold. It is then stood upright to drain, rested a little and cut across in strips, so that the crust stays crisp.

intro.what: This crumbed-cutlet method deep-fries the cutlet whole, then drains it upright before slicing.
intro.why: It teaches you to protect a crisp crust through moderate frying heat, draining and gentle cutting.

how: Heat deep oil in a heavy pan to a moderate heat, enough to cover the cutlet.
Test it with a few flakes of panko, which should sink briefly and then rise in a stream of fine bubbles.
Lower in one cutlet at a time, so that the oil keeps its heat, and leave it alone until the crust has set.
Turn it once and fry until the crust is deep gold on both sides.
Lift it out and stand it upright against a rack, so that the oil drains from the crust instead of pooling under it.
Rest it for a short while, then cut across in strips with a sharp knife, sawing lightly so that the crust does not shatter.

cues.text: A steady, lively sizzle that softens as the cutlet browns.
An even, deep gold crust, with the bubbles around it slowing down.

mistakes.mistake: Frying in oil that is too hot, so that the crust browns before the meat is ready.
mistakes.fix: Keep the heat moderate and test with a few flakes of panko.

mistakes.mistake: Laying the fried cutlet flat on a plate, where it steams and the crust goes soft.
mistakes.fix: Stand it upright against a rack.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting at once, so that the juice runs out and the crust goes limp.
mistakes.fix: Let it rest for a short while first.

quiz.question: Why stand the fried cutlet upright to drain?
choices: So the crust sits in its draining oil.
So oil runs off instead of pooling under the crust.
So the underside softens before slicing.
quiz.because: A flat cutlet can steam in pooled oil; upright draining helps its crust stay crisp.

quiz.question: How do you check the oil before adding the cutlet?
choices: Panko stays pale at the bottom without bubbling.
Panko turns dark immediately on contact.
Panko sinks briefly then rises with fine bubbles.
quiz.because: The brief sinking and rising test matches the moderate frying heat used here.

quiz.question: Which appearance matches the intended crust?
choices: Even deep gold on both sides.
A black crust with pale patches.
A pale coating that looks saturated with oil.
quiz.because: Even gold is the intended crust colour, rather than rapid overbrowning or a greasy pale coating.

quiz.question: The crust shatters when sliced. What would you change?
choices: Press straight down hard with a blunt knife.
Use a sharp knife with a light sawing motion after resting.
Tear the cutlet apart before draining.
quiz.because: Resting and gentle sawing avoid crushing the brittle crust while cutting strips.

comes_after.why: The crust must be on the meat before it goes into the oil.

variant_of.differs: One thick, crumbed piece of meat is fried whole at a moderate heat and turned once, then stood upright to drain, rested and cut across, where deep-frying works on small pieces and is salted at once.
